result.title: ConDenseDrive: Knowledge-Dense, Token-Sparse Visual Encoder for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
result.summary: End-to-end driving requires rich spatiotemporal representations to support scene understanding and trajectory planning under strict latency constraints. However, most systems initialize their visual encoders from generic image pretraining and densely process all patch tokens for each camera view and input frame, limiting both representation quality and inference efficiency. To address these challenges, we present ConDenseDrive, a knowledge-dense and token-sparse visual encoder for end-to-end autonomous driving. Our three-stage framework first makes the encoder knowledge-dense by distilling complementary visual, semantic, and geometric knowledge from three vision foundation models. It then adapts the distilled encoder to multi-frame end-to-end driving and integrates spatiotemporal context into register tokens for planning. Finally, it makes the encoder token-sparse by applying register-guided token compression, reducing redundant patch computation and yielding a 2.0$\times$ speedup while improving planning performance. ConDenseDrive achieves 94.5 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 90.8 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, and reaches 37.4 HD-Score in zero-shot evaluation on HUGSIM. Extensive experiments and qualitative analyses demonstrate that visual encoder design provides an effective route to reliable and efficient end-to-end driving.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ConDenseDrive，一个面向端到端自动驾驶的视觉编码器：先从三个视觉基础模型蒸馏视觉、语义与几何知识，再用 register token 承载多帧时空上下文，最后通过 register 引导的 token 压缩减少冗余 patch 计算，在 NAVSIM 与 HUGSIM 上评测规划性能与加速比。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 register token 汇聚时空上下文、并据此压缩 patch token 的设计，与 LVR 中「哪些视觉细节需留在内部状态、压缩是否导致信息坍缩」的问题结构相近，可供核查 token 稀疏化后任务必要信息的保留情况与成本收益，但属远领域线索，需人工判断可迁移性。
